alignments.note: Indefinite article belongs to the noun that licenses it (rule 15).
Verb rendered as light verb plus complement; heads on the complement under rule 44. Discontinuous around the negative determiner (rule 25).
The clause's negation is recast onto the nominal as the determiner 'no' (rule 15).

כִּי אִם fused as 'But only' under rule 35; the two English words are one rendering of the pair and neither morpheme owns a part of it (rule 30). No morpheme carries content the other lacks, so the head is the governing first morpheme (rule 23). Splitting 'But' from 'only' was the competing reading (rule 8).
Preposition before an infinitive construct recast as a finite clause takes the complementizer (rule 52).
Infinitive keeps its modal and lexical verb, with the reflexive realizing the Hithpael voice (rules 52, 44). The unit interleaves with the suffix and noun under rule 25.
Pronominal suffix rendered by a possessive (rule 18).

review_notes: The 'no' of 'hath no delight' is the negative's, and the light verb 'hath' stays with the verb whose complement 'delight' is.
